chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabala and others, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) emancipated the mischievous ones from his slaves at the time of his death, and retained the good ones. So I said, 'O father! You are freeing these and retaining those.' He said, 'They had been subjected to discipline from me, so this is for that.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Abu Ja'far free the difficult slaves and keep the good ones?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (as) illustrates the practical application of *tadbir* (manumission upon death) within the Ahl al-Bayt's household management, prioritizing the removal of difficult personalities to maintain domestic harmony. The Imam’s explanation that 'this is for this' highlights a reciprocal relationship where the slave's past misconduct justifies the master's financial sacrifice for their freedom, reflecting a nuanced approach to social justice and mercy in Shia jurisprudence.
